name: ATMOSPHERE FURNACE
desc: Double-Walled Laboratory Inert Atmosphere Muffle Furnace system engineered for high-temperature thermal processing under controlled vacuum and gas-purged environments. Features a 12-liter internal hot-zone chamber delivering an intensive heating range up to 1200°C.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS ATMOSPHERE FURNACE is a high-performance double-walled inert atmosphere muffle furnace engineered for oxide-free thermal processing up to 1200°C under vacuum or controlled gas purge. Its 12-litre hot-zone chamber is insulated with high-purity 1430°C-rated fibrous alumina ceramic fiber board and heated by ultra-durable Fe-Cr-Al-Mo alloy wire elements, while an industrial-grade K-type thermocouple and advanced programmable microprocessor PID controller maintain thermal accuracy within ±1°C. The integrated stainless steel needle valves, rotary vane vacuum pump, dial vacuum gauge, and inline gas flow meter enable precise anaerobic loops using nitrogen, argon, or clean inert gases, preventing oxidation, decarburization, and contamination. This system is widely used by PhD researchers, materials scientists, metallurgists, chemists, and B.Sc/M.Sc students for high-temperature annealing, brazing, sintering, ashing, and heat treatment of oxygen-sensitive metals such as titanium, zirconium, stainless steels, and superalloys, as well as advanced ceramics, powder metallurgy compacts, metal injection molded parts, and 3D-printed components. It supports compliance with thermal processing standards such as ASTM E220 for thermocouple calibration and ISO/ASTM 52900 for additive manufacturing post-processing, making it essential for aerospace R&D, metallurgy, ceramics, and advanced materials laboratories.
sop: Ensure the furnace is placed on a stable, level bench with at least 30 cm clearance and the main power switch is OFF before loading.

Open the heavy-duty swing door by releasing the dual screw locks, load the sample or crucible into the 200 × 200 × 300 mm chamber, and close and lock the door securely to engage the door safety limit switch.
Connect the inert gas supply (nitrogen or argon) to the gas inlet and ensure the rotary vane vacuum pump is connected to the vacuum port with the silicone rubber tubing.
Switch ON the main power supply and turn ON the vacuum pump; open the vacuum needle valve slowly and evacuate the chamber to the desired vacuum level as shown on the dial gauge.

Close the vacuum valve and open the gas purge needle valve to introduce inert gas until the flow meter indicates the required purge rate; repeat vacuum-purge cycles at least three times to achieve a low-oxygen atmosphere.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.
If using a multi-step profile, program the ramp rate (0–15°C/min) and soak segments via the controller's 30-step memory before initiating the run.
Initiate the heating program and monitor the actual temperature and atmosphere flow; do not open the door while the chamber is above 200°C or under vacuum/purge.
After the soak segment is complete, allow the furnace to cool to below 200°C under inert gas flow before switching off the gas supply and vacuum pump.
Switch OFF the main power, open the door only after confirming the chamber is at safe handling temperature, and remove the sample using appropriate high-temperature tongs and PPE.

Safety Warning: Never process volatile, flammable, or explosive materials such as strong acids, solvents, or VOCs in this furnace; always verify inert gas purity and exhaust ventilation to prevent asphyxiation or fire hazards.
